name: FpuEscape
comment: Intel 8087 ESC opcodes (0xD8-0xDF) — 8 opcode bytes each followed by a ModR/M-shaped second byte that the FPU consumes. Phase 28.IO no-op stub (single FpuEscape format mask=0xF8 match=0xD8): consume the ModR/M byte + any displacement and advance IP, do nothing else. This is enough for real PC/XT BIOS POST FPU detection — BIOS runs FNINIT/FSTCW/CMP to probe for 8087 presence; with no actual FPU side-effect the BIOS reads back its pre-cleared scratch byte, the compare fails, and the equipment-flag FPU bit is cleared (correct semantics for an 8086 without 8087 socketed). Real arithmetic, transcendentals, load/store land in Phase 29.2+.

formats.name: FpuEscape
formats.comment: 0xD8-0xDF — 8087 FPU escape prefix. Phase 28.IO no-op stub: consume the ModR/M byte (and any disp it implies via has_modrm=true at the decoder level) and advance IP, but do nothing else. This unblocks real BIOS POST which probes for FPU presence via FNINIT/FLDCW. Without FPU emulation the BIOS detection will see 'no FPU' and skip FPU-related branches, which is correct behavior for an 8086-class machine without an 8087.
